questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which patient is at risk for graft-versus-host disease?
choices: A patient receiving only their own autologous stem cells
A patient receiving an allogeneic donor stem cell transplant
A patient receiving a routine red-cell transfusion
A patient having a diagnostic bone marrow biopsy
questions.explanation: GVHD occurs when donor immune cells recognize recipient tissues as foreign, so it is a complication of allogeneic transplant rather than autologous cell return.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which post-allogeneic-transplant pattern most strongly suggests possible acute GVHD?
choices: New diffuse rash, watery diarrhea, and rising bilirubin
Stable weight with improving appetite
An isolated old bruise with normal counts
A healed central-line dressing
questions.explanation: Skin, gastrointestinal tract, and liver are common acute GVHD targets. Infection and medication toxicity must also be evaluated, so the transplant team needs prompt notification.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Three days after CAR-T infusion, a patient has fever, hypotension, and increasing oxygen need. What is the priority interpretation?
choices: This proves infection is impossible
This is expected and requires no escalation
Possible CRS with simultaneous evaluation for sepsis
This is isolated ICANS without systemic toxicity
questions.explanation: Fever with hypotension or hypoxia after immune effector therapy suggests CRS, but infection can coexist and appear similar. Activate both protocol-driven toxicity and infection evaluation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which subtle finding may be an early clue to ICANS?
choices: A patient suddenly cannot name familiar objects or write a sentence
A stable appetite after lunch
An unchanged chronic scar
A normal respiratory rate with intact attention
questions.explanation: Language, attention, and writing changes can precede more obvious neurotoxicity. Compare with the pre-infusion baseline and promptly repeat the standardized neurologic assessment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A CAR-T recipient becomes confused and has word-finding difficulty after fever improves. What should the RN do first?
choices: Assume recovery because the fever resolved
Delay assessment until the next scheduled shift
Give an unsupervised sedative
Urgently notify the cellular-therapy team, repeat the neurologic assessment, and use seizure and aspiration precautions
questions.explanation: ICANS may occur after CRS improves. New language or cognitive change requires immediate escalation, standardized assessment, and safety precautions while other causes are evaluated.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which cluster is concerning for sinusoidal obstruction syndrome after HSCT?
choices: Weight loss, low bilirubin, and increased urine output
Rapid weight gain, ascites, right-upper-quadrant discomfort, and rising bilirubin
Improving platelets with stable kidney function
Isolated mild alopecia
questions.explanation: Fluid retention, hepatomegaly or right-upper-quadrant discomfort, ascites, rising bilirubin, thrombocytopenia, and organ dysfunction form a concerning sinusoidal-obstruction pattern.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Why are cultures and empiric antibiotics often prepared during suspected CRS?
choices: CRS and sepsis can coexist and have overlapping findings
CRS permanently prevents bacterial infection
Every fever after CAR-T proves a line infection
Antibiotics are the primary treatment for isolated ICANS
questions.explanation: Fever, hypotension, and organ dysfunction can reflect CRS, infection, or both. Infection evaluation and timely prescribed antimicrobial treatment should proceed with the toxicity pathway.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which trend best indicates improvement during treatment of severe cellular-therapy toxicity?
choices: Increasing oxygen and vasopressor support with worsening attention
Stable fever alone despite new seizure
Decreasing support needs with improving cognition, perfusion, and oxygenation
One normal blood pressure while urine output falls
questions.explanation: Improvement is multidimensional: respiratory and circulatory support should decrease while neurologic function, perfusion, organ function, and urine output stabilize.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient after allogeneic transplant develops profuse diarrhea. Which nursing action is safest?
choices: Give an antidiarrheal independently before assessment
Assume GVHD is confirmed without testing
Measure and describe output, assess hydration, and promptly notify the transplant team for GVHD and infection evaluation
Stop all immunosuppression immediately
questions.explanation: Diarrhea may reflect GVHD, infection, conditioning injury, or medication toxicity. Quantify the trend, assess stability, and follow the transplant team's diagnostic and treatment plan.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement shows correct CAR-T discharge understanding?
choices: I will follow my product-specific monitoring and proximity plan and report fever or any speech, writing, or confusion change immediately
I can drive home whenever I feel awake after infusion
Fever is harmless unless it lasts several days
Once my blood counts rise, no long-term follow-up is needed
questions.explanation: CAR-T recipients need product- and center-specific monitoring, proximity, driving, and emergency instructions. Fever and subtle neurologic changes require immediate contact.
